newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to spend four trillion drachmas on defence.
newsitem.headline: Greece to spend four trillion drachmas on defence.

text.p: Greece will spend four trillion drachmas ($16.83 billion) by 2007 to upgrade its armed forces but the huge investment plan will not affect its European Union convergence targets, Prime Minister Costas Simitis told reporters.

"The total cost of the mid-term programme for the development and modernisation of the armed forces comes to about four trillion in current prices," he said after a meeting of the national defence council (KYSEA).
Greece has said it needs to boost its defence power to face a perceived threat from neighbouring Turkey. The two NATO members almost went to war over an uninhabited Eastern Aegean islet in January.
Asked if Greece would resort to foreign borrowing to cover the cost of the plan, Simitis said: "Yes, there will be borrowing to raise the funds."
He said the first two trillion would be spent by the year 2000 and the rest by 2007.
The programme includes one AWACS plane, 60 new fighter jets, modernising existing F4 Phantoms, new tanks, transport helicopters, submarines and nine new warships, he said.
It also includes missiles, anti-aircraft systems and trainer aircraft, he said.
"The cost will not affect our convergence plan with the EU," Simitis added.
The ministers of defence, national economy, finance and public works participated in the KYSEA meeting. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
